mission.title: Install and Configure k0s (Zero Friction Kubernetes)
mission.description: k0s is a lightweight, all-inclusive Kubernetes distribution designed for ease of use and quick deployment. It is ideal for cloud, bare metal, and edge environments, offering a single binary for installation. Key trade-offs include simplicity at the cost of advanced features found in other distributions.

steps.title: Install k0s CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the k0s command-line interface, which is necessary for managing your Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

curl -sSL https://get.k0s.sh | sudo sh

```

> This command downloads and installs the latest k0s binary.

steps.title: Initialize the k0s Controller
steps.description:
This step initializes the k0s controller, which will manage the Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

sudo k0s install controller

```

> This command sets up the controller on the host.

steps.title: Start the k0s Controller
steps.description:
This step starts the k0s controller service, allowing it to manage the Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

sudo k0s start

```

> This command starts the k0s controller.

steps.title: Configure kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step sets up the kubeconfig file, which allows you to interact with your Kubernetes cluster using kubectl.

```bash

sudo k0s kubeconfig admin > ~/.kube/config

```

> This command generates the kubeconfig file for the admin user.

steps.title: Verify the Cluster
steps.description:
This step checks that the cluster is running correctly and that the nodes are ready.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> This command lists all nodes in the cluster and their status.

uninstall.title: Uninstall k0s
uninstall.description:
This step removes the k0s installation and all associated resources. Be aware that this will delete all cluster data.

```bash

sudo k0s stop

sudo k0s uninstall

```

> Stops the k0s controller.
> Uninstalls k0s and removes all resources.

upgrade.title: Upgrade k0s
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you backup your cluster data. This step performs the upgrade and verifies the installation.

```bash

sudo k0s stop

curl -sSL https://get.k0s.sh | sudo sh

sudo k0s start

kubectl get nodes

```

> Stops the k0s controller before upgrading.
> Re-installs the latest k0s binary.
> Starts the k0s controller after the upgrade.
> Verifies that all nodes are in a ready state after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'k0s: command not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The k0s CLI is not installed or not in the PATH.

**Fix:**
Reinstall k0s using the installation command.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'no nodes available in cluster'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The k0s controller is not running or nodes are not joined.

**Fix:**
Check the status of the k0s controller and ensure nodes are properly joined.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'kubeconfig file not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubeconfig file is not generated or is in the wrong location.

**Fix:**
Run 'sudo k0s kubeconfig admin > ~/.kube/config' to generate the kubeconfig file.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'context deadline exceeded'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The Kubernetes API server is not reachable.

**Fix:**
Check the network configuration and ensure the k0s controller is running.

versionNotes.changes: Improved support for multi-node installations and enhanced security features.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: Run 'k0s upgrade' to migrate from previous versions.

resolution.summary: You should see a list of nodes with the status 'Ready' when running 'kubectl get nodes'.
